steps.why: this is WHY the right wing is forced one-sided, and it is honest about what the left wing costs. The total angle deficit is a topological invariant: sum_v (12 - 2*deg_v) = 12*chi (Gauss-Bonnet, 14.B.4). The icosahedral sphere has the twelve degree-5 sites contributing 12*(+2) = +24 = 12*chi, so chi = 2 (genus 0). A surface that is negatively curved EVERYWHERE (all deg > 6, every (12-2d) < 0) must have sum < 0, hence chi < 0 -- a closed genus >= 2 surface, or the non-compact (open) hyperbolic plane. It CANNOT be a genus-0 sphere. This is exactly why container 15.C.2 found the sphere one-sided (D >= 0): on a closed genus-0 surface Gauss-Bonnet PINS the net curvature at +12*chi = +24 > 0, so it cannot be net-negative -- the left wing simply does not fit on the same surface. The two signs are not two regions of one sphere; they are two topologies. (This is the curvature-total statement only -- NOT a claim about which surface the substrate 'is'.)
